title: Keeping Up with Science: We’re Losing 338 Spoken Words Every Day

elements.content: Welcome to Keeping Up with Science. Review the research context and metadata below:

Session Overview:
• Duration: 60 minutes
• Languages: 🇬🇧 🇫🇷 🇪🇸 🇮🇹 🇷🇺
• Level: Intermediate (B1)
• Topic: Sociolinguistics / Digital Communication
• Resources: Full Article 📖

Specimen / Topic
Language Attrition & Cognition

Primary Hypothesis
Digital screen saturation accelerates native lexical attrition.

Experimental Findings
Speech variety in teenagers has contracted by 15% over a 10-year study.

Linguistic Focus
Passive voice vs Active voice in news.

Do you talk more or type more during an average day?
Who is the most "talkative" person you know?
Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

• Linguistic Decay: the gradual loss of words or grammatical structures in a language over time.
   Example: "Some experts are concerned about linguistic decay caused by rapid texting."

• Interaction: reciprocal action or influence between two or more people.
   Example: "Face-to-face interaction is essential for maintaining social skills."

• Monosyllabic: consisting of one syllable (often used to describe short, unhelpful answers).
   Example: "He gave a monosyllabic reply when I asked how his day was."

• Cognitive Load: the amount of information that working memory can hold at one time.
   Example: "Deep conversation requires a higher cognitive load than simple messaging."

• Eloquence: fluent or persuasive speaking or writing.
   Example: "His eloquence made him a very effective public speaker."

• Vocabulary Range: the total number of different words a person knows and uses.
   Example: "Reading diverse books is the best way to expand your vocabulary range."

• Isolation: the state of being separate from others.
   Example: "Physical isolation is highly linked to cognitive decline in older seniors."

• Nuance: a subtle difference in meaning, expression, or sound.
   Example: "A rich vocabulary allows you to express every small nuance of emotion."

• Digital Distraction: losing focus on a task or conversation because of a digital device.
   Example: "Digital distraction is often cited as a cause for shorter real-life conversations."

• Interpersonal: relating to relationships or communication between people.
   Example: "The company is looking for candidates with strong interpersonal skills."

🗣️ Task 2 : Interactive Speaking:
Should the decay of traditional languages be actively fought by schools, or is it a natural change?
Analyze the core scientific findings and discuss the personal prompts in pairs:

• According to the research, what specific parameters indicate that a rapid linguistic decay is taking place in modern communities?

• What evidence in the study shows that face-to-face interaction is crucial to prevent the erosion of rare words?

• According to researchers, what are the cognitive risks of a purely monosyllabic verbal habit in teenagers?

• Based on the clinical observations, how does texting minimize the overall cognitive load during social communication?

• How does the study map the correlation between standard reading habits and verbal eloquence?

• What data metrics prove that our overall vocabulary range has contracted significantly over the last decade?

• According to the paper, how does physical isolation accelerate native language attrition?

• What findings show that young speakers are losing their appreciation for conversational nuance?

• How do scientists isolate the effects of digital distraction from general sociolinguistic evolution during testing?

• What parameters define successful interpersonal communication in the study's experimental setup?

elements.content:
❌ There is less words today ➔ ✔️ There are fewer words today (Fewer for countable nouns)
❌ It is a very good news ➔ ✔️ It is very good news (Uncountable news)
❌ I am agree with you ➔ ✔️ I agree with you (Verb agreement)
❌ It is depend on you ➔ ✔️ It depends on you (Verb vs Adjective)
